## Overview

**Paul** was a priest of Aurelius and a warrior of the **Order of the Protectors**. He raised **Aegon** as his own son after the boy was orphaned, trained him in the ways of the paladin, and ultimately died for knowing too much. His death is the catalyst that set Aegon on his path as the Rogue Paragon.

---

## Appearance

A gentleman in his forties at the time of his death. Kind-faced, with the weathered hands of a warrior and the calm eyes of a man who had seen much. He wore simple priestly robes over well-worn armour  -  a man equally at home in a chapel or on a battlefield.

---

## Background

Little is known of Paul's life before he became a priest. His history and identity before joining the Order remain a mystery. What is known is that he was no ordinary clergyman  -  he possessed an uncanny ability to detect truth from lies, was highly skilled in combat, and carried himself with the discipline of a true warrior. He belonged to the **Order of the Protectors**, the knightly sub-chapter of the Order of the Scales.

When the infant Aegon was brought to his chapel  -  orphaned, mother dead from childbirth, father vanished  -  Paul accepted him without hesitation. He raised the boy as his own, training him in combat, faith, and the principles of justice. He recognized early that Aegon was special  -  blessed with healing powers, magical sensitivity, and prophetic visions.

Paul revealed the truth to Aegon: he was a **Paragon**, a paladin with an extraordinary connection to the divine. He guided Aegon through his training and saw him swear the oath at the High Septon.

### The Shift

In his final years, Paul's own visions began to change. Where once he heard only Aurelius, a new voice began to whisper  -  older, stranger, carrying truths the gods did not want spoken. B's lingering consciousness in the Weave was reaching out to him.

Paul realized what Aurelius truly was: not a benevolent god, but a fragment of something older and far more dangerous. He understood that the Order of the Scales unknowingly served a false divinity. And he knew that this knowledge meant his death.

### Death

Paul was killed in his own chapel  -  not by the Crimson Covenant, as the official story claims, but by agents of the Order of the Scales acting on divine command from Aurelius himself. The Covenant was framed to hide the truth.

As he lay dying in Aegon's arms, he spoke his final words:

> *"Do not trust the Order... Trust your oath and your visions..."*

He died knowing Aegon would one day understand.

---

## Abilities

- **Paladin's Skills**: Combat mastery, healing, divine magic
- **Truth-Seeing**: An uncanny ability to detect lies  -  likely a form of divine magic (Zone of Truth, Discern Lies)
- **Vision-Touched**: Received prophetic visions  -  first from Aurelius, then from B's consciousness in the Weave

---

## Relationships

- **Aegon**  -  Adopted son and student. Paul raised him, trained him, and died warning him.
- **The Order of the Protectors**  -  His knightly chapter. His brothers and sisters in arms.
- **The Order of the Scales**  -  The order he served. The order that killed him.
- **Aurelius**  -  The god he once served faithfully. The god who ordered his death when he learned too much.
